ui_surface: Dominant shipped pattern across mainstream coding editors: voice is an affordance OF the existing chat/agent panel, delivered as an INLINE MICROPHONE BUTTON inside the chat input box of that panel — never a floating overlay or drawer. VS Code puts a mic button + Voice Mode button in the chat input (and in the Agents window/editor/terminal inputs); Cursor puts a mic icon in the chat input; Replit puts the mic in the Agent chat box; Windsurf puts voice input in the Cascade agent panel; JetBrains Air puts a mic button in the Chat task input. Cursor 3.1 adds only lightweight recording chrome (waveform/timer/cancel-confirm) docked at that same input. No studied editor mounts voice as a position:fixed overlay — the sanctioned surface is the chat dock/panel or (for dictation) the editor/terminal input itself.
shipped_status: SHIPPED as voice INPUT (speech-to-text into the chat input, user reviews/sends) in: Cursor (Cursor 2.0, 29 Oct 2025; reworked in 3.1), VS Code/Copilot Chat (built-in dictation + experimental Voice Mode; plus the VS Code Speech extension), Cascade in Windsurf/Devin Desktop, Replit Agent (Voice Mode), and JetBrains Air (local Whisper). SHIPPED as voice OUTPUT (TTS of agent responses) only in: VS Code Voice Mode (reads responses aloud) and the VS Code Speech extension (autoSynthesize); the Cursor 'Bot' voice chat also speaks, but that is a separate bot surface, not the coding-agent chat. DOCUMENTED-BUT-NOT-SHIPPED for the agent: Zed (roadmap 'Hands-Free Coding' listed under Currently Working On; dictation/Voice Input requests still in Triage; issue #16410 open since Aug 2024). NOT SHIPPED: JetBrains AI Assistant and Junie have no first-party dictation (AI Chat docs describe typed prompts only); an IntelliJ mic exists only via third-party plugins. INFERRED/community: exact injection semantics for Windsurf voice and Cursor's submit-keyword auto-send.
findings: PRIMARY (given the DSH reject-overlay verdict): every mainstream editor that ships voice treats it as part of the chat/agent panel, not a competing surface. VS Code's Voice Mode button and mic live in the chat input; its docs say Voice Mode 'sends your request to the active chat or agent session and uses its selected model and attached files' and it 'announces when it routes a request to an existing session or starts a new one' — i.e. voice is a front-end to the sanctioned session, not a separate overlay. URL: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/accessibility/voice

VS CODE (a) voice in/out: ships BOTH. Experimental Voice Mode = hands-free spoken conversation AND reads the agent's responses aloud (agents.voice.speakResponses; agents.voice.handsFree re-listens after the agent speaks). Built-in dictation (on-device model `nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b` on desktop by default) is speech-to-text only. The VS Code Speech extension adds speech-to-text + text-to-speech for chat responses + 'Hey Code' keyword activation for platforms without built-in dictation. URLs: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/accessibility/voice ; https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode.vscode-speech

VS CODE (b) how spoken text enters the session: dictation 'inserts text in the input but does not submit the request' — effectively identical to the user typing it, and the user presses Enter. Voice Mode instead acts as the user's request: it sends the spoken request to the active chat/agent session and can auto-start a new session. Neither is attributed to a separate author — it is a normal user prompt. URL: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/accessibility/voice

VS CODE (c) surface: inline mic button in the chat input (+ Voice Mode button in chat input), plus dictation into the Agents window chat input, into writable editors (a mic control appears at the cursor), and into terminals; shortcut ⌘I in chat, ⌥⌘V in editor; Voice Mode ⇧⌘Space. Recording chrome is a context menu on the Voice Mode button / chat-input controls — no overlay. URLs: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/accessibility/voice ; https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/reference/copilot-vscode-features

VS CODE (d) extension API surface #1 — Chat Participants API: register with `vscode.chat.createChatParticipant(id, handler)` and declare `contributes.chatParticipants` in package.json; the handler receives `ChatRequest`, `ChatContext`, `ChatResponseStream`, `CancellationToken` and can write to the panel via stream.markdown/button/reference/progress/filetree/push(part). Participants access history (only turns where they were mentioned) as `ChatRequestTurn | ChatResponseTurn`. URLs: https://code.visualstudio.com/api/extension-guides/chat ; https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/contribution-points

VS CODE (d) extension API surface #2 — Language Model API: `vscode.lm.selectChatModels(...)` then `model.sendRequest(messages, options, token)`; messages are built from `LanguageModelChatMessage.User(...)` / `.Assistant(...)` only (docs: the API does not support system messages). This lets a voice extension generate content but returns it to the extension, not into the built-in chat transcript. URLs: https://code.visualstudio.com/api/extension-guides/language-model ; https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/contribution-points

VS CODE (d) extension API surface #3 — Chat Sessions API (PROPOSED, in `vscode.proposed.chatSessionsProvider.d.ts` + the `chatSessions` contribution point): `registerChatSessionContentProvider(scheme, provider, defaultChatParticipant, capabilities)`, `registerChatSessionItemProvider`/`createChatSessionItemController`, and `provideChatSessionContent(...)` returns a `ChatSession` whose history is `ChatRequestTurn2 | ChatResponseTurn2`. This is the deepest way for an extension to own/stream a session transcript into the native chat UI, but it is a proposed API (requires `enabledApiProposals`). URLs: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat/blob/main/src/extension/vscode.proposed.chatSessionsProvider.d.ts ; https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatSessions/chatSessions.contribution.ts

VS CODE (d) extension API surface #4 — the chat-input command: `vscode.commands.executeCommand('workbench.action.chat.open', { query, isPartialQuery })`. With isPartialQuery:true it prefills the chat input and waits for the user (the standard 'starter prompt' pattern); with isPartialQuery:false the implementation calls `acceptInput()` and submits. There is also `chatUtils.sendChatParticipantRequest(...)` to invoke a participant programmatically. This is the documented mechanism a voice extension would use to write into a chat session as if typed. URLs: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-discussions/discussions/2480 ; https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/99489178/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/actions/chatActions.ts ; https://code.visualstudio.com/api/extension-guides/ai/chat

VS CODE (d) transcript provenance — the chat history model DOES distinguish message kinds, on a request-vs-response axis, not a 'voice vs typed' axis. `ChatRequestTurn` is documented as 'Represents a user request in chat history' (fields: prompt, participant = the participant it was directed to, command, toolReferences). `ChatResponseTurn` is 'Represents a chat participant's response in chat history' (fields: participant = the participant it came FROM, command, response parts, result). So a response is attributed to the producing participant/extension; a request is modelled as the user's. URLs: https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/vscode-api ; https://code.visualstudio.com/api/extension-guides/chat

VS CODE (d) provenance nuance: the proposed `ChatRequestTurn2` adds `readonly isSystemInitiated?: boolean` — documented as 'Whether this request was initiated by the system rather than the user.' So the model can flag a non-user-initiated request, but there is no general-purpose author/provenance label (e.g. 'voice') and no supported way to inject a message that persists in the built-in transcript as a distinct author other than the user or a named participant. URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/vscode/main/src/vscode-dts/vscode.proposed.chatParticipantPrivate.d.ts

VS CODE (d) LM-API role model: the internal `ChatMessageRole` enum is System/User/Assistant, and the LM API exposes only `LanguageModelChatMessage.User`/`.Assistant` (system messages unsupported via the API). That is the full author vocabulary available to an extension building prompts; 'voice' is not a role. URLs: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/languageModels.ts ; https://code.visualstudio.com/api/extension-guides/language-model

VS CODE (d) related contribution points listed in the reference: `chatAgents`, `chatInstructions`, `chatPromptFiles`, `chatSkills`, `languageModelTools`, `languageModelChatProviders` (note: the contribution-points reference index does not list `chatParticipants`, although the Chat Participant guide shows declaring it — a docs quirk; treat `chatParticipants` as valid per the guide). URL: https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/contribution-points

CURSOR (a) voice in/out: ships voice INPUT. Cursor 2.0 (29 Oct 2025) changelog — 'Voice Mode: Control Agent with your voice using built-in speech-to-text conversion. You can also define custom submit keywords in settings to trigger the agent to begin running.' No documented voice OUTPUT for the coding agent chat. Cursor separately ships a spoken 'voice chat with a Bot' (Bot replies out loud) — a different surface. URLs: https://cursor.com/changelog/2-0 ; https://cursor.com/help/grok-bot/voice-chat

CURSOR (b) injection: the transcription lands as ordinary text in the chat input. Docs: 'Click the microphone icon in the chat input to dictate your prompt instead of typing... review the transcription before sending.' Voice Mode can additionally auto-run via user-defined submit keywords (from the 2.0 changelog). So the spoken result enters the input box as if the user typed it (review-first), with an optional keyword-triggered send — not attributed to a separate author. URLs: https://cursor.com/docs/agent/prompting ; https://cursor.com/changelog/2-0

CURSOR (c) surface: inline microphone icon in the chat input; Cursor 3.1 'Upgraded voice input' added recording UI at that input (waveform, timer, cancel/confirm) and hold-Ctrl+M to talk; keyboard shortcut page lists 'Cmd Shift Space — Toggle Voice Mode'. Cursor release notes note a 'Live microphone meter while dictating... into the agent input'. No overlay. URLs: https://cursor.com/changelog/3-1 ; https://cursor.com/docs/reference/keyboard-shortcuts ; https://cursor.com/docs/release-notes/ide

WINDSURF/CODEIUM (Cascade) (a)(b)(c): official docs state 'Voice input — Use Voice input to use your voice to interact with Cascade. In its current form it can transcribe your speech to text.' Voice input lives in the Cascade agent panel (opened with Cmd/Ctrl+L); input only, no documented voice output; the exact injection point (chat box) is implied by the docs and stated by third parties. Product has been rebranded (Windsurf → Devin Desktop); the same docs serve docs.windsurf.com and docs.devin.ai. URLs: https://docs.windsurf.com/windsurf/cascade/cascade ; https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/cascade ; https://docs.devin.ai/windsurf/plugins/cascade/cascade-overview

ZED (a) voice for the agent is NOT shipped. Official roadmap lists 'Hands-Free Coding — Voice commands and built-in calling for a more accessible workflow' under 'Currently Working On' (in progress, not shipped), and the Triage section still carries 'Voice Input with Voice Activation to Chat in Zed' and 'Dictation for Assistant (inline and chat-based)'. Issue #16410 has been open since 2024-08-17. URLs: https://zed.dev/roadmap ; https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/16410

ZED (b)(c): no shipped mic for dictation; proposals in the tracker ask for a mic/push-to-talk button in the Agent Panel composer that inserts editable, reviewable text before submit (so the same 'text into the input' pattern). The only shipped microphone is voice chat for collaboration Channels — a human-to-human call mic in the upper-right of the window, explicitly NOT dictation. URLs: https://zed.dev/docs/collaboration/channels ; https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/16410

JETBRAINS (a)(c): AI Assistant and Junie ship no first-party voice. The official AI Chat docs describe typed prompts with attached context and no microphone. JetBrains' separate agentic product 'Air' DOES ship voice input: 'Voice input uses a local Whisper model... no audio is sent to the cloud', configured in Settings → Voice Input, then 'click the microphone button in the task input and dictate the task'. Voice output is not documented. URLs: https://www.jetbrains.com/help/ai-assistant/ai-chat.html ; https://www.jetbrains.com/help/air/define-tasks.html

REPLIT AGENT (a) voice in only, explicitly no out: 'Voice Mode... Tap the microphone in the Agent chat box... transcribes your speech into editable text.' Docs: 'It does not read Agent's responses aloud.' URL: https://docs.replit.com/features/agent/voice-mode

REPLIT (b)(c): transcription 'inserts the result into the chat box for you to review before sending... nothing is sent automatically', and 'the transcript appears as regular text in the chat box, so you can mix voice and typing freely' — again the insert-as-if-typed pattern. Surface: microphone button inside the Agent chat box (inline mic), recording shown by a waveform; available in the Project Editor and the home-screen Agent prompt, on desktop web/mobile web/mobile app. URL: https://docs.replit.com/features/agent/voice-mode

CROSS-CUTTING PATTERN (the key takeaway for dsh-openai-live): no mainstream editor introduces a NEW top-level surface for voice. Voice is (1) an inline mic in the chat input that inserts reviewable text as if the user typed it (Cursor, Replit, Windsurf, JetBrains Air, VS Code dictation), and/or (2) a 'voice mode' that submits a spoken user request into the existing session and optionally speaks the reply (VS Code Voice Mode; Cursor Bot voice chat). Attribution stays 'the user' or 'the producing participant'; 'voice' is not a transcript author. URLs: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/accessibility/voice ; https://cursor.com/docs/agent/prompting ; https://docs.replit.com/features/agent/voice-mode
unverified: Windsurf/Cascade: whether the transcription is inserted as editable text the user reviews before sending, or auto-submitted — the official docs only say it 'can transcribe your speech to text' (inferred, not documented). See https://docs.windsurf.com/windsurf/cascade/cascade

Cursor: exact submit-keyword behavior (does a spoken keyword auto-send the prompt, and does the message appear as a normal user turn) is stated in the 2.0 changelog but not detailed in docs; community threads assert 'Speech-to-text just populates the normal chat input, so it counts the same as if you had typed the message yourself'. URL: https://forum.cursor.com/t/cursor-voice-input/152878

Cursor: whether Voice Mode / the improved 3.1 voice pipeline is available in the main Cursor window chat or only the Agents window — a Cursor community thread claims it is Agents-window-only; not confirmed in official docs. URL: https://forum.cursor.com/t/cursor-3-1-tiled-layout-and-upgraded-voice-input/157293

JetBrains: the claim that AI Assistant/Junie voice is tracked as open YouTrack issues (e.g. JUNIE-796, LLM-1562, IJPL-217393) came from a third-party dictation-vendor blog, not from a YouTrack page I read directly; the primary evidence I verified is only that the official AI Chat doc shows no microphone. URL: https://www.jetbrains.com/help/ai-assistant/ai-chat.html

VS Code Speech extension details (Ctrl+I press-and-hold-to-submit, 26 languages, accessibility.voice.autoSynthesize) are from the Marketplace listing/wiki, which may lag the shipped-built-in-dictation docs; note the built-in dictation (dictation.enabled, on-device model) supersedes the extension on supported desktop platforms per https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/accessibility/voice

VS Code: `chatParticipants` appears in the Chat Participant guide's package.json example but NOT in the contribution-points reference index (which lists chatAgents/chatSkills/etc.); I did not find a primary page reconciling whether both contribution points coexist today. URLs: https://code.visualstudio.com/api/extension-guides/chat ; https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/contribution-points

Whether any mainstream editor lets an extension persist a message into the built-in chat transcript attributed to a NON-user, NON-participant author (e.g. labelled 'voice'): I found no documented API for this. The closest are ChatSessionContentProvider (own the whole session), a participant response turn (attributed to the participant), or workbench.action.chat.open (prefill/submit the user's input). This absence is an inference from the API surfaces reviewed, not an explicit statement. URLs: https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/vscode-api ; https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat/blob/main/src/extension/vscode.proposed.chatSessionsProvider.d.ts

Third-party mentions of Claude Code /voice, Warp terminal voice, and various system-wide dictation layers are out of scope for the five named editors and were not verified against primary vendor docs.
